assessment.nobel_worthiness: A major theoretical and computational breakthrough that made realistic binary black-hole waveforms and their interpretation possible, enabling a new form of astronomy.
assessment.attribution: The credited names represent complementary advances: effective-one-body theory and numerical relativity. Their contributions are distinct and central, though the later observational achievement depended on large experimental collaborations.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been tested extensively against gravitational-wave observations and remains essential to waveform modeling.
uncertainties: The division of credit between foundational theory, numerical breakthroughs, and later waveform development is difficult to capture in three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson completed a central test of the Standard Model and stands among the defining achievements of particle physics.
assessment.attribution: These leaders represent the two experiments and the sustained detector and collaboration work behind the discovery. The result was collective, so individual attribution is necessarily incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The discovery has been independently established by ATLAS and CMS, with subsequent measurements confirming the particle's properties.
uncertainties: A prize to a few individuals would only partially represent the thousands of contributors to the experiments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of pulsars opened a new observational window on neutron stars and produced a lasting set of tools for testing gravity and studying dense matter.
assessment.attribution: Bell Burnell's role in identifying the first pulsar signal was decisive and merits direct recognition.
assessment.maturity: Pulsars have been observed for decades across many systems, and their physical interpretation is secure.
uncertainties: The broader scientific legacy spans many later discoveries, but the initial discovery itself has clear attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The identification of neutron-star mergers as sites of heavy-element production connected gravitational-wave astronomy with the origin of the elements and established a powerful form of multimessenger astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: The credited names span key theoretical interpretation and observational work on the kilonova. The contribution of James Lattimer to the earlier merger-nucleosynthesis prediction also makes the listed attribution incomplete.
assessment.maturity: The 2017 neutron-star merger provided strong direct evidence, and subsequent work has strengthened the case, though the relative contribution of mergers to the full r-process inventory remains under study.
uncertainties: The size of the merger contribution to cosmic heavy-element abundances is not yet fully settled.
Credit spans predictions, transient interpretation, and observations by large collaborations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos established neutrino astronomy and opened a new way to study energetic cosmic sources.
assessment.attribution: Halzen's scientific leadership and Spiering's sustained work on the detector and field are important, while the discovery depended on a large international collaboration.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux is established and source associations have begun, but the population and acceleration mechanisms are still being mapped.
uncertainties: The individual credit for a collaboration-scale detection is difficult to assign.
The astronomical picture enabled by the discovery is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light turns quantum optics into a practical route to improved precision measurement and has increased the sensitivity of gravitational-wave observatories.
assessment.attribution: The names cover the theoretical proposal, influential experimental development, and application to interferometric measurement. Roman Schnabel and many detector teams also made substantial contributions.
assessment.maturity: The technique is operating in gravitational-wave detectors and its benefits are measured directly.
uncertainties: The discovery is a long chain of theory, laboratory demonstrations, and detector implementation, making the boundary of the prize contribution debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The titanium-sapphire laser and practical passive mode locking made robust femtosecond pulses broadly accessible, transforming ultrafast science and applications.
assessment.attribution: Moulton's laser development and the distinct mode-locking advances associated with Keller and Sibbett provide a strong, focused attribution.
assessment.maturity: The technology has been used and refined for decades and remains a foundational ultrafast light source.
uncertainties: The field includes multiple important designs and subsequent improvements, so the exact scope of a prize would need careful definition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks have advanced precision measurement by orders of magnitude and provide new tests of fundamental physics as well as a basis for future time standards.
assessment.attribution: Katori and Ye independently developed leading approaches that drove the field forward; their complementary contributions support joint recognition.
assessment.maturity: The performance is repeatedly demonstrated across laboratories, with comparisons and applications already underway.
uncertainties: The ultimate metrological and fundamental-physics impact is still growing, and other groups have made important contributions to the field.
